papers.title: Toward quantum scaling advantage in approximate optimization
papers.access: Full v2 HTML and supplement; arXiv history confirms first 28 May 2025, v2 10 July 2026; Phys Rev Applied 26,014024 DOI10.1103/qcws-8kgm.
papers.sections_reviewed: Main methods/results/discussion, Figs1–5; supplement S1–S7, particularly S1,S2,S5,S6.
papers.defensible_result: GPU simulated bifurcation closes the reported scaling gap on the same Sidon-28 QAC instances under the studied timing definitions.

objections.claim_under_test: General quantum or industrial optimisation advantage/disadvantage
objections.evidence: Main comparison uses125 random instances per size on QAC-native graphs,142–1322 logical variables; larger classical-only study uses10 per size2380–38320.
objections.locator: Thermal vs Chaotic vs Quantum Annealing; S2
objections.consequence: A strong counter-baseline for this ensemble; not a theorem about general optimisation.

objections.claim_under_test: Better multi-GPU scaling means faster practical service
objections.evidence: Four-GPU total times are approximately100 times one-GPU times at studied small sizes, despite improved fitted exponents. Common initialization omitted; GPU compute time averages parallel resources.
objections.consequence: Separate exponent, actual latency and hardware/resource budget.

objections.claim_under_test: Large-size asymptotic or future quantum scaling is established
objections.evidence: Finite-range fits and optimum-parameter searches;3D points outside search range excluded. Larger quantum counterpart not measured.
objections.consequence: Future overhead-free advantage remains a candidate, not demonstrated.

papers.what_survives: A credible instance-matched rebuttal to a particular claimed quantum scaling gap, with unusually explicit runtime accounting.
papers.what_would_resolve: Broader held-out ensembles, matched full workflow/resource costs, certified reference energies at large sizes and quantum measurements beyond current size range.
papers.verdict: Survives with narrow scope; no central numerical result disproved.

papers.title: A Reality Check on Quantum Optimisation: Evidence from an Industrial Case Study
papers.access: Full v1 HTML; first submitted14 July2026; no journal reference on opened arXiv record.
papers.sections_reviewed: SectionsI–IX, formulationsIII, setupV, all resultsVI and validityVII.
papers.defensible_result: On the studied industrial assignment-based scheduling formulations, the Digital Annealer handles larger instances and beats the implemented greedy/iterative approximations in schedule quality; current quantum devices struggle with feasibility.

objections.evidence: V-C calls the metric end-to-end; VII-E explicitly excludes communication, API overhead and queues.
objections.consequence: The end-to-end label is false; operational timing advantage is not established.

objections.evidence: V-A certifies only up to6machines5rigs14jobs; larger references are best found within one hour, despite later true-optimal/lower-bound wording.
objections.locator: V-A; VII-A; Fig8 caption and VI-D
objections.consequence: Use best-known gaps at larger sizes; no certified approximation guarantee.

objections.evidence: Native greedy/SDST insertion/iterated-greedy is included, so not merely QUBO-vs-QUBO; however comparison uses100–1200iterations and equal quadratic scaling language rather than equal measured total budgets.
objections.consequence: A useful case study does not establish superiority over tuned native state-of-art solvers.

objections.claim_under_test: Full job-shop optimisation and DA as lower bound for future quantum
objections.evidence: Models omit internal job order; sequencing delegated to classical stage and mean setup proxies used. DA constraint handling differs physically.
objections.consequence: Retain assignment-workflow value; reject generic quantum performance projection.

papers.what_survives: Evidence that formulation and constraint handling dominate this particular practical benchmark; actual quantum feasibility limits remain meaningful.
papers.what_would_resolve: Matched wall-clock native MILP/CP/heuristic benchmarking, certified bounds where feasible, full pipeline timing and transparent returned-sample accounting.
papers.verdict: Useful preprint case study; qualified classical comparator and corrected timing/optimality labels essential.

papers.title: Field Demonstration of Distributed Quantum Sensing without Post-Selection
papers.access: Full journal PDF opened,14 July2021; local arXiv2011.02807v1 also inspected but journal takes precedence.
papers.sections_reviewed: JournalI–IV, Figs1–3; AppendicesA–D resource/loss accounting; journal result for AppendixE comparator.
papers.defensible_result: At240m fibre length, distributed optical phase estimation beats the loss-accounted photon-pass SNL by up to0.916dB; journal additionally reports0.326dB without multipass weighting.

objections.evidence: Six random-phase estimates with10km spools explicitly fail to beat SNL because of efficiency.
objections.consequence: Do not combine240m advantage with10km reach into one result.

objections.evidence: Parameter is controlled waveplate optical phase; setup needs polarization calibration and synchronized photon detection;10km uses spools.
objections.consequence: Outdoor distribution is genuine; defence target sensing or deployed network is untested.

objections.claim_under_test: Coincidence analysis automatically invalidates no-postselection claim
objections.evidence: Lost photons and multipair events enter resource estimate Eq2; Bob multipasses counted twice; lossless optimal allocation defines SNL. JournalA includes visibility and59.1% threshold.
objections.consequence: Concern is rebutted by explicit resource accounting; no demonstrated loophole.

objections.claim_under_test: Gain over every optimized classical or unentangled strategy
objections.evidence: Comparator is photon-pass shot-noise bound with no multipassing; source, detector infrastructure and elapsed acquisition cost are not the resource metric. Journal separately demonstrates ordinary two-sensor weighting.
objections.consequence: Claim specific SNL improvement; not system-cost superiority over all sensor architectures.

papers.what_survives: Strong field proof of resource-accounted photonic metrology within a defined estimation task.
papers.what_would_resolve: Unknown physical-signal tests, stable long-distance advantage, acquisition-bandwidth and complete infrastructure comparisons.
papers.verdict: Central result survives; restrict range/application and use journal rather than older preprint numbers.

papers.title: Quantum locking of intrinsic spin squeezed state in Earth-field-range magnetometry
papers.access: Saved publisher full HTML; supplementary PDF downloaded/read Notes1–8; published3March2025.
papers.sections_reviewed: All main Results/Discussion/Methods; supplement SQL,spin dynamics,entanglement,pulse timing and robustness.
papers.defensible_result: A theoretical/numerical pulse-control proposal aligns and preserves intra-atomic spin squeezing, predicting metrological gain in an Earth-field model.

objections.evidence: Discussion says proposed and supposes1cm3 cell,N=1.42e10,T2=10ms; sensitivity follows model versus5.99fT/√Hz CSS SQL.
objections.consequence: Label predicted sensitivity, not experimental demonstration.

objections.claim_under_test: Below total sensor noise in realistic field
objections.evidence: Gain measures spin variance divided by mean spin; Faraday readout/backaction considered theoretically but no measured total-noise spectrum or hardware comparison.
objections.consequence: Spin-noise advantage is conditional on readout/technical noise control.

objections.claim_under_test: Robust autonomous tracking in variable fields
objections.evidence: B0 fixed with small perturbation; calculated1pT single-shot uncertainty versus±50pT gain window. Pulses require instantaneous-rotation/RWA timing constraints; supplementary timing-deviation robustness reoptimizes sequence for each deviation.
objections.consequence: Does not establish robustness to unknown fast dynamics or implementation errors.

objections.claim_under_test: No interatomic entanglement means no quantum resource
objections.evidence: Main text explicitly uses nuclear-electronic entanglement within each atom; supplement derives entropy. Gain independent of atom number.
objections.consequence: Reject this objection; clarify resource and absence of improved N scaling.

papers.what_survives: Interesting control proposal converting nonlinear Zeeman dynamics into usable intra-atomic squeezing; not field-tested instrument.
papers.what_would_resolve: Experimental squeezing/readout calibration, total-noise benchmark versus optimized CSS protocol, finite pulse and changing-field tests.
papers.verdict: Retain as theory proposal with conditional metrological promise; downgrade any demonstrated-sensitivity claim.

papers.title: Superextensive electrical power from a quantum battery
papers.access: Saved publisher full HTML;32page supplement downloaded and pertinent device,ultrafast and electrical sections read; published13March2026.
papers.defensible_result: Eight CuPc microcavity devices show cavity-enhanced photon-to-charge conversion and increasing cavity/control electrical power ratio under steady illumination; ultrafast spectroscopy supports collective charging dynamics.

objections.claim_under_test: Conventional complete storage battery cycle and net efficiency
objections.evidence: Electrical output obtained from steady625nm illumination10mW/cm2 I–V scans; reported output10–40µW/cm2. Stored excitations observed optically on nanosecond scales.
objections.consequence: Not delayed electrical discharge after charging, cycle life or round-trip storage efficiency; inferred incident-light conversion is roughly0.1–0.4%, not round-trip efficiency.

objections.claim_under_test: Measured universal N-squared output law and sqrtN voltage
objections.evidence: MainFig4d fits cavity/control ratio as N changes with composition; S17 actual voltage fitN^0.77 excludes anomalousD4; S19 qualitative model assumes selected transport energies/rates.
objections.consequence: Finite device family and model do not certify asymptotic exponent or universal advantage.

objections.claim_under_test: Pure N variation isolates collective quantum advantage
objections.evidence: CuPc:C60 ratio/layer thicknesses and cavity detuning vary; paired controls and fixed-average-cavity modelling are meaningful rebuttals, but not an experimental fixed-composition scaling family.
objections.consequence: Confounds are partially addressed, not proven responsible or fully eliminated.

objections.claim_under_test: Nonclassical resource proven necessary for electrical improvement
objections.evidence: Spectra fitted by coupled oscillators; quantum transport model reproduces trends qualitatively; no witness or resource-removal comparison establishes entanglement necessity.
objections.consequence: Do not equate strong coupling with certified nonclassical computational/metrological advantage.

papers.what_survives: Substantive cavity optoelectronics result including real electrical output, beyond optical charging alone.
papers.what_would_resolve: Independent devices, fixed-composition/geometry resource-normalized controls, delayed electrical extraction and cycles, measured net efficiency, decisive nonclassical-resource test.
papers.verdict: Electrical enhancement credible; practical battery and uniquely quantum advantage claims exceed demonstrated evidence.
